hero.headline: From curiosity to dashboard
hero.subheadline: I'm João Vitor — a data analyst in the making, turning questions into visualizations that help you decide.

about.title: About
about.label: // WHO I AM
about.paragraph1: I started my career in administrative work — managing inventory and building spreadsheets. Along the way I realized: what interests me most isn't the spreadsheet itself, it's the question that comes before it.
about.paragraph2: Today I'm studying Business Process Management and learning data analysis hands-on — building public dashboards with real data, making mistakes, adjusting, publishing. Every project here started as a curiosity and became a visualization.
about.paragraph3: I don't call myself an expert. I call myself someone who's building, in public.

projects.title: Projects
projects.label: // PROOF OF WORK
projects.subtitle: Four projects built with real data. Each one started with a question.

financeiro.title: Financial Analysis
financeiro.subtitle: Personal P&L
financeiro.tagline: A profit & loss statement, but personal
financeiro.description: Personal finance control dashboard with monthly revenue and expense tracking, categorization and balance indicators.
financeiro.question: How do you visualize personal financial health beyond just the bank balance?
financeiro.approach: I organized income and expense data into categories, built a monthly timeline and calculated balance indicators. The structure follows the logic of a corporate P&L, adapted for a personal context.
financeiro.data_source: Fictional data structured based on real household spending patterns.
learnings: Expense categorization reveals patterns that the final balance hides.
Visualizing monthly trends is more useful than looking at a snapshot.
Keeping the structure simple makes continuous updating easier.

people_analytics.title: People Analytics
people_analytics.subtitle: HR with data
people_analytics.tagline: What the data says about the team
people_analytics.description: HR dashboard with headcount, turnover, department distribution and engagement indicators.
people_analytics.question: How do you present HR data so managers quickly understand the state of the team?
people_analytics.approach: I structured metrics in layers: overall headcount view, then turnover by period, then department distribution. The order follows the logic of someone who asks 'how many of us are there?' before 'who left?'.
people_analytics.data_source: Synthetic data built from public HR market benchmarks.
learnings: The order of indicators matters as much as the indicators themselves.
Turnover without context of growth or hiring is incomplete data.
Distribution charts reveal imbalances that averages hide.

ecommerce.title: E-commerce Sales
ecommerce.subtitle: Online sales
ecommerce.description: Commercial performance analysis of an e-commerce operation — best-selling products, buying behavior and revenue evolution.
ecommerce.question: Which products drive revenue and which purchase patterns repeat?
ecommerce.approach: I analyzed sales data by product, channel and period. I crossed average ticket with volume to identify products that are worth more than they seem and those that seem more than they're worth.
ecommerce.data_source: Synthetic dataset based on retail e-commerce patterns.
learnings: Best-selling product isn't necessarily the most profitable.
Seasonality appears clearly when you group by week, not month.
Average ticket by category says more about the customer than the product.

ibovespa.title: Brazilian Market
ibovespa.subtitle: B3 · Ibovespa 2024
ibovespa.description: Overview of the Brazilian financial market in 2024 — Ibovespa performance, macroeconomic context and key events of the year.
ibovespa.question: What happened to the Brazilian financial market in 2024 and how do the main indicators relate?
ibovespa.approach: I collected verified data from primary sources (Central Bank of Brazil, Agência Brasil, InfoMoney), organized it on a timeline and contextualized index movements with corresponding macroeconomic events.
ibovespa.data_source: Banco Central do Brasil, Agência Brasil, InfoMoney. Verified and referenced data.
learnings: Public financial data requires cross-validation between sources.
Contextualizing numbers with events makes the dashboard analytical, not just descriptive.
The Ibovespa in 2024 reflected domestic fiscal conditions more than external ones.
